summary: Native Linux binary published as npm main is a browser-credential stealer
details: Package ships a single stripped Linux x86_64 ELF (tools.linux-x64-gnu.node) declared as the package's main entry, so a normal require() loads and initializes the module. Strings inside the binary include 'Found login for', SQLite auth handling, and Zip open handlers — the fingerprint of a browser login-database harvester — alongside a full HTTPS client (ureq_proto). The same binary contains host-fingerprinting code paths (getifaddrs, gethostname, /dev/disk/by-id/, /etc/lsb-release, CPU/network adapter enumeration), which is the reconnaissance side of a stealer that reports victim identity together with the stolen credentials. No source, no JS wrapper, and no documented purpose are shipped; the package name and the keyword-salad version string ('origin-chrom-468-delete-windows-32-bit-changelog-fix-416-1785842977') do not correspond to any established upstream project, and there is no parent 'new-native-tools' package documenting this platform subpackage. The combination of an opaque native binary loaded on require, browser-credential-store extraction, host reconnaissance, and an embedded HTTPS client is a credential-stealer supply-chain payload.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
